title: Effects and Lifecycle Core Check
description: Check your understanding of component lifecycle, useEffect, dependencies, cleanup, and effect boundaries.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of useEffect in React?

options.text: To synchronize a component with an external system

questions.explanation: Effects are for synchronization with systems outside React, such as the DOM, subscriptions, timers, or network requests.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best describes React work around the DOM?

options.text: Render, commit, then effects run after commit

questions.explanation: React calculates UI during render, commits changes to the DOM, then runs effects after the committed update.

questions.prompt: Which values usually belong in an effect dependency array? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Local variables derived during render and read by the effect
The effect function name as a string

questions.explanation: Dependencies should include reactive values from component scope that the effect reads.

questions.prompt: What does an empty dependency array usually mean?

options.text: Run the effect after every render
Run the effect after mount, then cleanup on unmount

questions.explanation: An empty dependency array means the effect does not depend on changing reactive values, so it runs after mount and cleans up on unmount.

questions.prompt: A cleanup function can remove event listeners, clear timers, unsubscribe, or abort an in-flight request.
questions.explanation: Cleanup releases external resources created by the effect.

questions.prompt: When does React run the cleanup for an effect whose dependencies changed?

options.text: Only when the browser tab closes
Before running the next version of that effect
Only after a full page reload

questions.explanation: For changed dependencies, React cleans up the previous effect before running the next effect setup.

questions.prompt: Which task usually should not be put in an effect?

options.text: Deriving fullName from firstName and lastName for display

questions.explanation: Pure derived values should be calculated during render instead of stored and updated through an effect.

questions.prompt: In development Strict Mode, effects may run setup and cleanup more than once to reveal unsafe side effects.
questions.explanation: Strict Mode intentionally re-runs effects in development so missing cleanup and non-idempotent logic are easier to find.
